# AES Core Behavioral Specification

## 1. Scope

This specification defines the behavioral requirements for the AES core module. The module implements the AES block cipher engine for AES-128, AES-192, and AES-256, and supports the ECB, CBC, CFB-128, OFB, and CTR operating modes. It is responsible for accepting configuration, key material, initialization vectors, and input data, and for producing output data, status information, and alert indications.

The specification covers the register interface, entropy interfaces, cipher operation, and masked-data handling.

---

## 2. Functional Overview

The module must:

- Perform AES encryption and decryption of 128-bit data blocks.
- Support AES-128, AES-192, and AES-256 key lengths when so configured.
- Support the following cipher modes:
  - ECB
  - CBC
  - CFB with a fixed 128-bit data segment size
  - OFB
  - CTR
- Accept the initial key in two shares, with the actual key equal to the bitwise XOR of the shares.
- Optionally accept an initial key from a sideload key source instead of from software.
- Generate all round keys internally from the initial key.
- Provide automatic or manually triggered block operation.
- Provide status indication for idle, input readiness, output validity, and stalling.
- Clear sensitive key, IV, and data storage with pseudo-random data when requested or during de-initialization.
- Detect and report recoverable and fatal fault conditions.

---

## 3. Software-Visible Behavior

### 3.1 Configuration

The module must hold the following configuration information:

- Operation direction: encryption or decryption.
- Cipher mode: ECB, CBC, CFB, OFB, or CTR.
- Key length: 128, 192, or 256 bits.
- Key source: software-provided key shares or sideload key.
- Operation mode: automatic or manual.
- Optional control for forcing masking randomness to zero, only when permitted by build configuration.

The control configuration must be shadowed. A configuration update shall take effect only after software writes the same value twice. If the two writes do not match, the module must:

- Not apply the new configuration.
- Retain the previous valid configuration.
- Assert a recoverable control-update alert condition.

The module shall ignore writes to the control, key-share, and IV storage while it is not idle. Software must check that the module is idle before reconfiguring it.

### 3.2 Key Material

The key is always supplied as two share containers. Each share container consists of eight 32-bit words. The actual key is the bitwise XOR of the two share containers.

For AES-128, the key is the XOR of the first four 32-bit words of each share container. For AES-192, it is the XOR of the first six words. For AES-256, it is the XOR of all eight words.

Independent of the selected key length, software must write all eight 32-bit words of both share containers at least once before the key is considered ready. The unused words are ignored by the cipher operation, but they must still be written. Random data is preferred for unused words.

When a sideload key is selected:

- Writes to the software key-share storage must be ignored.
- The module must use the key provided by the sideload source.
- In automatic mode, the module must not start a block operation using the sideload key until the sideload source indicates that the key is valid. Manual start bypasses this readiness check; software must ensure valid material before requesting it.

The module must generate all AES round keys internally from the initial key. Software does not supply round keys.

If the selected operation is ECB or CBC decryption and the key has changed, the module must first perform a decryption key-scheduling setup before it can begin the first data block. During this setup, the module must not be idle and must not accept or start a data block operation.

### 3.3 Initialization Vector and Counter

In CBC, CFB, OFB, and CTR modes, a 128-bit IV must be provided through four 32-bit IV storage locations. In ECB mode, the IV is not used.

The IV must be considered ready only when either:

- All four IV words have been written at least once since the last IV update or clear, or
- None of the IV words have been written since the last IV update, meaning the internally updated IV is already valid.

The module must not start a block operation with a partially updated IV. If software writes only some IV words, the module shall wait until either all four words have been written or the IV is cleared/reloaded.

The module may update IV storage automatically during CBC, CFB, OFB, and CTR operation, as required by the cipher mode.

### 3.4 Input Data

The input data block is supplied through four 32-bit input data locations. A complete input block requires all four locations to have been written at least once since the previous input block was consumed. The order of writes does not matter.

The module must indicate when it is ready to accept a new input data block. When ready, writes to the input data storage must be accepted without disturbing the current operation. When not ready, input data writes shall not be treated as a valid complete block.

### 3.5 Output Data

The output data block is provided through four 32-bit output data locations. The module must indicate when a new output block is available.

A complete output block is considered consumed only after all four output data locations have been read at least once since the block was produced. The order of reads does not matter.

In automatic operation mode:

- The module must not overwrite an output block that has not been fully read.
- If a new output block is ready and the previous output block has not been consumed, the module must stall rather than drop or overwrite data.
- The module must indicate that it is stalled in this condition.

In manual operation mode:

- The module must not stall waiting for output data to be read.
- A new output block may overwrite a previous unread output block.

### 3.6 Status Indication

The module must provide status information to software indicating at least:

- Whether the module is idle and ready for reconfiguration.
- Whether new input data can be accepted.
- Whether output data is valid and available to be read.
- Whether the module is stalled waiting for output data to be consumed.
- Whether recoverable or fatal alert conditions have been recorded.

### 3.7 Trigger Actions

The module must provide software-triggerable actions for:

- Manually starting an operation.
- Clearing key, IV, and input data storage with pseudo-random data.
- Clearing output data and internal output state with pseudo-random data.
- Requesting a reseed of the internal pseudo-random number generators.

Trigger requests must be consumed by the hardware and automatically cleared when the requested action is performed.

---

## 4. Block Operation

### 4.1 Automatic Operation

In automatic operation mode, the module shall start a block operation when all of the following conditions are true:

- The control configuration is valid and has been successfully updated.
- The initial key is ready.
- If the selected mode requires an IV, the IV is ready.
- A complete input data block has been written.
- The module is not busy with a previous operation, key setup, clear operation, or reseeding operation.
- In automatic mode, unread output data prevents completion and output-register replacement; it does not itself prevent launching the next cipher operation.

Once a block operation starts, the module must load the input block, perform the appropriate AES operation, and produce the output block.

While processing a block, the module may accept the next input data block if input-ready is indicated.

### 4.2 Manual Operation

In manual operation mode:

- The module must not start automatically simply because input data and IV are present.
- Software must explicitly request a start.
- The start request must be cleared automatically when the operation begins.
- The module does not wait for input data or IV readiness before honoring a start request.
- The module does not stall to protect unread output data.

Software is responsible for ensuring that valid key material, IV, and input data are present before requesting a manual start.

### 4.3 Reset and Initialization

The main storage and control use rising-edge clocking and active-low asynchronous reset. Key-share, IV, previous-input, and output registers reset to zero. The controller resets to idle; reset does not itself run a full random-storage-clear sequence. The shadowed control storage also has rst_shadowed_ni. Software must establish a valid configuration and the required key, IV, and input data before automatic processing. Explicit clear and reseed requests are serviced by the controller.
---

## 5. Cipher Mode Behavior

The following definitions are used:

- \(D\): the input data block.
- \(Y\): the output data block.
- \(K\): the AES key.
- \(IV\): the current IV, counter, or feedback value.
- \(IV'\): the IV, counter, or feedback value to be used for the next block.
- \(E_K\): AES encryption.
- \(D_K\): AES decryption.

The module must implement the following mode behavior.

### 5.1 ECB

Encryption:

\[
Y = E_K(D)
\]

Decryption:

\[
Y = D_K(D)
\]

The IV is not used and must not affect the operation.

### 5.2 CBC

CBC encryption:

\[
Y = E_K(D \oplus IV)
\]

\[
IV' = Y
\]

CBC decryption:

\[
Y = D_K(D) \oplus IV
\]

\[
IV' = D
\]

For CBC decryption, the next IV is the ciphertext block, which is the input data block of the current operation.

### 5.3 CFB-128

CFB encryption and decryption both use the forward AES encryption operation on the IV value:

\[
Y = D \oplus E_K(IV)
\]

The next IV must be the previous ciphertext block:

- For encryption, the input data block is plaintext and the output data block is ciphertext, so \(IV' = Y\).
- For decryption, the input data block is ciphertext and the output data block is plaintext, so \(IV' = D\).

### 5.4 OFB

OFB encryption and decryption both use the forward AES encryption operation on the IV value:

\[
Y = D \oplus E_K(IV)
\]

\[
IV' = E_K(IV)
\]

### 5.5 CTR

CTR mode uses a 128-bit counter value. The initial counter value is the IV.

Encryption and decryption both use the forward AES encryption operation on the counter value:

\[
Y = D \oplus E_K(CTR)
\]

After each block, the counter must be incremented by 1 modulo \(2^{128}\):

\[
CTR' = CTR + 1 \pmod{2^{128}}
\]

The counter increment must treat the 128-bit value as a big-endian integer.

---

## 6. Randomness, Masking, and Clearing

### 6.1 Pseudo-Random Generation

The module must have access to pseudo-random data for:

- Clearing sensitive registers and state.
- Masking the cipher data path when masking is enabled.

The randomness used for clearing and the randomness used for masking must be separate.

The clearing generator starts from its configured LFSR seed. Software reseed requests initiate the entropy handshake and take priority over data-update requests. While a reseed is being serviced the controller does not start a new operation. SecSkipPRNGReseeding suppresses the external clearing entropy request and acknowledges the reseed internally.

### 6.2 Masking Behavior

When masking is enabled:

- The module must process key and state material in masked form.
- The module must generate masking randomness internally.
- The module must use masking randomness when creating masked shares for each new block operation.
- The module must not expose masked intermediate values as output.
- The final output data must be the unmasked cipher result.
- Before cipher output validity has the canonical asserted encoding, each share entering output recombination shall carry its corresponding clearing-generator data. Separate share streams shall be used. When validity is canonically asserted, the shares shall carry the final cipher state and their XOR shall produce the unmasked state. Invalid validity encodings select clearing data. This rule concerns internal combinational share handling; it does not mark software output registers valid.
- The clearing streams are derived from the configured clearing LFSR and share permutation; no statistical independence between them is promised.

When masking is disabled, the module must still accept the key in two shares. The two shares must be combined internally to produce the actual key for the unmasked cipher operation.

### 6.3 Clearing Behavior

The module must provide the following clearing behavior:

- A key/IV/input-data clear request must overwrite all key share storage, IV storage, input data storage, and previous-input-data storage with pseudo-random data.
- An output-data clear request must overwrite output data storage and internal output state with pseudo-random data.
- Any clear operation must complete before the module becomes idle again.
- No new block operation may start while a clear operation is in progress.
- A clear operation must not cause valid output data to be signaled as newly available.

Sensitive key and data storage must not be cleared to deterministic zero values as the primary clear mechanism.

---

## 7. Alert and Fault Behavior

### 7.1 Recoverable Alerts

A recoverable alert condition must be reported if a control configuration update error is detected.

On a recoverable control-update error:

- The module must assert the recoverable alert indication.
- The module must record the condition in status.
- The module must continue operating with the previous valid configuration.
- The recorded status may be cleared by a subsequent control register write.
- A recoverable alert must not require a reset.

### 7.2 Fatal Alerts

The module must treat the following conditions as fatal faults:

- An invalid encoding detected on internal control or data-path selector signals.
- An internal counter inconsistency.
- A cipher-core internal alert condition.
- A control-path terminal error state.
- A life-cycle escalation indication.
- An externally supplied integrity error indication.
- A shadowed control-storage error, including one that later disappears; this condition is latched until reset.

When any fatal fault is detected:

- The module must assert the fatal alert indication.
- The fatal alert indication must remain asserted until reset.
- The module must record the fault in status.
- The module must stop starting new operations.
- The module must not release any further output data.
- Any operation in progress must be abandoned or held such that no additional output is produced.

A fatal fault requires a reset to clear.

---

## 8. Build-Time Configuration Effects

The module’s behavior may be modified by build-time configuration. The following behavioral differences must be supported:

- AES-192 support may be disabled. An AES-192 selection then maps to AES-256; unsupported key-length encodings also map to AES-256. Unsupported mode encodings map to AES_NONE and prevent cipher start.
- Masking may be disabled. When disabled, the module does not perform masked cipher operations, but the external key-share interface remains two-share.
- The S-Box implementation may be selected at build time. This may affect performance and latency but must not change the functional behavior described in this specification.
- A start-trigger delay may be configured. When configured, manual start requests are honored after the configured delay.
- External PRNG reseeding may be skipped. In that configuration the generators use their configured seeds, and software reseed requests do not require external entropy.
- Forcing masking randomness to zero may be enabled. When enabled, software may set a control bit to disable random masking. This is intended only for controlled use and must not be available unless explicitly enabled.

The output-lost status records overwrite of unread data in manual mode. Fatal alert status updates clear recoverable control-update status. Register word order and state conversion treat each 32-bit word as one AES state column; IV storage is updated in 16-bit counter slices. Key and data write enables accept only the canonical asserted sparse encoding. Invalid selector encodings select safe defaults and contribute to terminal control fault handling.
